Consistent with previous studies, our meta-analysis supports the
beneficial effects of EX on blood pressure reduction [119–121]. How­
ever, the effectiveness of EX may be influenced by factors such as indi­
vidual characteristics, EX type, and intensity. For example, a
meta-analysis focusing on adults with different hypertensive states
found that endurance training had the greatest reduction in blood
pressure in hypertensive individuals, whereas dynamic resistance
training had a modest but non-significant effect in those with pre­
hypertension [122]. Another research found that moderate-intensity
resistance training significantly reduced blood pressure, while
low-intensity interventions did not find this association [123]. Due to
the limited number of studies for each exercise type, we were unable to
perform subgroup analyses in the prehypertensive population. Future
research should focus on identifying the most effective EX modalities for
optimal outcomes in prehypertension.
Our results suggest that combining multi-component lifestyle in­
terventions
